```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```


The goal of this document is to get you up and running with `multiLocalFDR` as quickly as possible. 

# Installation

```{r warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval=FALSE}
library(devtools)
install_github("JungiinChoi/multiLocalFDR", ref = "LogConcDEAD")
```

You can install multiLocalFDR from the Github directory. 
For Mac users, you need to install Xcode before the installation. 
(If Xcode is not installed, R automatically redirects you to install XCode.)

# Main Functions

## SPMix()

```{r eval=FALSE}
SPMix <- function(z, tol = 5e-6, p_value = FALSE, alternative = "greater", max_iter = 30, mono = TRUE, thre_z = 0.9, Uthre_gam = 0.9, Lthre_gam = 0.01 )
```

* z: Given matrix which column indicates raw data. 
* tol: tolerance value for determining convergence of EM-type algorithm
* p-value: if TRUE, than we assume that the input is p-value $\in [0,1]$.
* alternative: if 'greater', than it assumes alternative distribution is greater than (on the right side of) null density. This applies for only univariate data.

## plotSPMix()

```{r eval=FALSE}
plotSPMix <- function(z, p0, mu0, sig0, f, f1, localFDR, p_value = FALSE,
                      alternative = "greater", thre_localFDR = 0.2, testing = TRUE,
                      xlab = "x", ylab = "y", coord_legend = c(8, -5, 0.2))
```

* testing: If TRUE, the visualization is for hypothesis testing, otherwise, density estimation.

# Simulations

In this section, we will use __SPMix()__ to estimate mixture density and compute local-FDR for generated data. Also, __plotSPMix()__ can visualize the fitted results
for both univariate and 2-dimensional data. 

## required libraries

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(copula)
library(mclust)
library(mvtnorm)
library(ggplot2)
library(scatterplot3d)
library(multiLocalFDR)
```

```{r echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(LogConcDEAD)
library(logcondens)
library(stats)
library(graphics)

SPMix <- function(z, initial_p0 = 0.5, tol = 5.0e-5, is_pvalue = FALSE,
                  alternative = NULL, min_iter = 3, max_iter = 50, 
                  Uthre_gam = 0.99, Lthre_gam = 0.01, thre = 0.4)
{
  # *****************DEFINITION OF INTERNAL FUNCTIONS ******************
  
  # Internal Functions
  fit_normal_mixture_1d <- function(z, p0, tol = 5e-3, max_iter = 5) {
    q0 <- quantile(z, probs = p0)
    
    # Compute initial estimates
    mu0 <- mean(z[z <= q0])
    sig0 <- sd(z[z <= q0])
    mu1 <- mean(z[z > q0])
    sig1 <- sd(z[z > q0])
    
    f0 <- dnorm(z, mean = mu0, sd = sig0)
    f1 <- dnorm(z, mean = mu1, sd = sig1)
    ell <- sum(log(p0 * f0 + (1 - p0) * f1))
    
    for (k in 1:max_iter) {
      gam <- p0 * f0 / (p0 * f0 + (1 - p0) * f1)
      
      # M-step
      p0 <- mean(gam)
      mu0 <- sum(z * gam) / sum(gam)
      sig0 <- sqrt(sum(gam * (z - mu0)^2) / sum(gam))
      f0 <- dnorm(z, mean = mu0, sd = sig0)
      
      mu1 <- sum(z * (1 - gam)) / sum(1 - gam)
      sig1 <- sqrt(sum((1 - gam) * (z - mu1)^2) / sum(1 - gam))
      f1 <- dnorm(z, mean = mu1, sd = sig1)
      
      new_ell <- sum(log(p0 * f0 + (1 - p0) * f1))
      if (k >= 3 && abs(new_ell - ell) <= tol) break
      ell <- new_ell
    }
    
    list(p0 = p0, mu0 = mu0, sigma0 = sig0, mu1 = mu1, sigma1 = sig1)
  }
  
  fit_normal_mixture_nd <- function(z, p0, tol = 5e-3, max_iter = 5) {
    require(mvtnorm)
    
    z <- as.matrix(z)
    n <- nrow(z)
    d <- ncol(z)
    q <- qnorm(p0)
    
    # Identify indices for the null and alternative distributions
    ind0 <- rowSums(scale(z) <= q) == d
    ind1 <- rowSums(scale(z) > -q) == d
    
    # Compute initial estimates
    mu0 <- colMeans(z[ind0, , drop = FALSE])
    sig0 <- cov(z[ind0, , drop = FALSE])
    mu1 <- colMeans(z[ind1, , drop = FALSE])
    sig1 <- cov(z[ind1, , drop = FALSE])
    
    f0 <- dmvnorm(z, mu0, sig0)
    f1 <- dmvnorm(z, mu1, sig1)
    f <- p0 * f0 + (1 - p0) * f1
    ell <- mean(log(f))
    
    for (k in 1:max_iter) {
      gam <- p0 * f0 / f
      
      # M-step
      p0 <- mean(gam)
      mu0 <- colSums(z * gam) / sum(gam)
      dev0 <- (z - mu0) * sqrt(gam)
      sig0 <- t(dev0) %*% dev0 / sum(gam)
      f0 <- dmvnorm(z, mu0, sig0)
      
      mu1 <- colSums(z * (1 - gam)) / sum(1 - gam)
      dev1 <- (z - mu1) * sqrt(1 - gam)
      sig1 <- t(dev1) %*% dev1 / sum(1 - gam)
      f1 <- dmvnorm(z, mu1, sig1)
      
      f <- p0 * f0 + (1 - p0) * f1
      new_ell <- mean(log(f))
      
      if (k >= 3 && abs(new_ell - ell) <= tol) break
      ell <- new_ell
    }
    
    list(p0 = p0, mu0 = mu0, sig0 = sig0, mu1 = mu1, sig1 = sig1)
  }
  
  select_NE <- function(x, X) {
    return(which(rowSums(X >= matrix(x, nrow = nrow(X), ncol = ncol(X), byrow = TRUE)) == ncol(X)))
  }
  
  monotone_fdr <- function(z, fdr) {
    apply(z, 1, function(row) max(fdr[select_NE(row, z)]))
  }
  
  # ******************* MAIN FUNCTION *******************************
  if (is_pvalue) {
    if (any(z <= 0 | z >= 1, na.rm = TRUE)) {
      warning("Some p-values are 0 or 1 and were clipped to avoid Inf/NaN in qnorm.")
    }
    z <- pmin(pmax(z, 1e-300), 1 - 1e-16)
    z <- qnorm(ifelse(is.null(alternative), 1 - z, z))
  }
  
  z <- as.matrix(z)
  n <- nrow(z)
  d <- ncol(z)
  ell <- rep(NA, max_iter)
  
  if (ncol(z) == 1) {
    raw_sd <- sd(z)
    raw_mean <- mean(z)
    z <- scale(z)
  }
  
  if (!is.null(alternative)) {
    for (j in 1:d) {
      if (!alternative[j]) {
        z[, j] <- -z[, j]
      }
    }
  }
  
  ## Initial step: to fit normal mixture
  if (d == 1) {
    z = z[,1]
    # Initial step: Fit normal mixture
    nmEM <- fit_normal_mixture_1d(z, p0 = initial_p0)
    p0 <- nmEM$p0
    f0 <- p0 * dnorm(z, mean = nmEM$mu0, sd = nmEM$sigma0)
    f1 <- dnorm(z, mean = nmEM$mu1, sd = nmEM$sigma1)
    f <- p0 * f0 + (1 - p0) * f1
  } else {
    ## Initial step: to fit normal mixture
    Params <- fit_normal_mixture_nd(z, p0 = initial_p0)
    p0 <- Params$p0
    mu0 <- Params$mu0
    sig0 <- Params$sig0
    f0 <- dmvnorm(z, mu0, sig0)
    f1 <- dmvnorm(z, Params$mu1, Params$sig1)
    f <- p0*f0 + (1 - p0)*f1
    ell[1] <- mean(log(f), na.rm = TRUE)
  }
  if (d == 1) {
    z <- as.numeric(z)
    ## EM-step
    k <- 0; converged <- 0
    while (k < max_iter) {
      k <- k + 1
      
      # E-step
      gam <- p0 * f0 / f
      
      # M-step
      weight <- gam / sum(gam, na.rm = TRUE)
      mu0 <- sum(weight * z, na.rm = TRUE)
      sig0 <- sqrt(sum(weight * (z - mu0)^2, na.rm = TRUE))
      f0 <- p0 * dnorm(z, mean = mu0, sd = sig0)
      p0 <- mean(gam, na.rm = TRUE)
      
      # Update gam
      gam <- p0 * f0 / f
      which.z <- gam <= thre
      weight <- (1 - gam[which.z]) / sum(1 - gam[which.z], na.rm = TRUE)
      f1 <- numeric(n)
      if (sum(which.z) >= 3) {
        z1 <- z[which.z] + rnorm(sum(which.z), sd = 1e-5 * sd(z[which.z]))
        lcd <- activeSetLogCon(x = z1, w = weight)
        f1[which.z] <- exp(lcd$phi)[order(order(z1))]  # safer than rank()
      } else {
        warning("Too few points in alternative region for log-concave estimation.")
        f1[which.z] <- 0
      }
      

      # Update f and log-likelihood
      f <- p0 * f0 + (1 - p0) * f1
      ell[k] <- mean(c(log(p0 * f0[!which.z]), log((1 - p0) * f1[which.z])))
      cat(".")
      
      # Check for convergence
      if (k >= 7) {
        diff <- abs(ell[k] - ell[k - 1])
        converged <- (diff < tol)
      }
      if (converged) {
        cat("Converged!\n")
        break
      }
    }
    
    if (!converged) cat("Warning: Not converged!\n")
    # Final posterior probabilities
    gam <- p0 * f0 / f
    ell <- na.omit(ell)
    
  } else {
    ## EM-step
    k <- 1; converged <- 0
    while ( (k < 5) | ((k < max_iter) & (!converged)) ) {
      k <- k + 1
      
      ## E-step
      gam <- p0 * f0 / f
      gam <- monotone_fdr(z, gam)
      
      ## M-step
      sum_gam <- sum(gam)
      mu0 <- as.vector(t(z) %*% gam) / sum_gam
      dev <- t(t(z) - mu0) * sqrt(gam)
      sig0 <- t(dev) %*% dev / sum_gam
      p0 <- mean(gam)
      f0 <- dmvnorm(z, mu0, sig0)
      f1 <- rep(0, n)
      which_z <- (gam <= thre)
      weight <- 1 - gam[which_z]
      weight <- weight/sum(weight)
      lcd <- mlelcd(z[which_z,], w = weight)
      f1[which_z] <- exp(lcd$logMLE)
      f <- p0*f0 + (1 - p0)*f1
      ell[k] <- mean(log(f), na.rm = TRUE)
      
      ## Update
      diff <- abs(ell[k] - ell[k - 1])
      converged <- (diff <= tol)
      cat(".")
      if (converged) {
        cat("Converged!\n")
        break
      }
    }
    if(!converged) cat("Warning: Not converged!\n")
  }
  
  if (!is.null(alternative)) {
    if (d == 1) {
      if (!alternative[1]) {
        mu0 <- -mu0
        z <- -z
      }
    } else {
      for (j in 1:d) {
        if (!alternative[j]) {
          mu0[j] <- -mu0[j]
          z[, j] <- -z[, j]
        }
      }
    }
  }
  
  
  # return results
  
  if (is_pvalue) {
    res <- list(z = z, p0 = p0, mu0 = mu0, sig0 = sig0, f = f, f1 = f1,  
                log.likelihood = ell,
                localFDR = gam, posterior = cbind(gam, 1 - gam),
                iter = k, dim = d, alternative = alternative,
                converged = converged)
  } else {
    if (d == 1){
      res <- list(z = z*raw_sd + raw_mean, p0 = p0, mu0 = mu0*raw_sd + raw_mean, 
                  sig0 = sig0*raw_sd, f = f/raw_sd, f1 = f1/raw_sd, 
                  log.likelihood = ell,
                  localFDR = gam, posterior = cbind(gam, 1 - gam),
                  iter = k, dim = d, alternative = alternative,
                  converged = converged)
    } else {
      res <- list(z = z, p0 = p0, mu0 = mu0, sig0 = sig0, f1 = f1, f = f,
                  iter = k, log.likelihood = ell, lcd = lcd, dim = d,
                  posterior = cbind(gam, 1 - gam), localFDR = gam,
                  converged = converged)
    }
  }
  class(res) <- "SPMix"
  return(res)
}
```

## Univaraite

### Normal + Normal

Let's consider randomly generated 1000 data from the density below. 

$$f = 0.8 \cdot N(0,1) + 0.2 \cdot N(3.5, 0.5^2)$$

```{r}
set.seed(1)

n <- 10000
p0 <- 0.8
n0 <- rbinom(1, n, p0)
n1 <- n - n0
z0 <- rnorm(n0)
z1 <- rnorm(n1, mean = 3, sd = 0.5)
z_NN1d <- c(z0, z1)

NN1d <- SPMix(z_NN1d)
str(NN1d)
```

__SPMix()__ returns null probability($p0$), null parameters($\mu_0, \sigma_0$), 
estimated density and nonnull density($f, f_1$) and estimated local-FDR value.

```{r}
# Hypothesis testing 
plotSPMix(NN1d)
```

__plotSPMix()__ can be used for both hypothesis testing and density estimation. 
If testing is TRUE (default), it gives density estimation for both normal and nonparametric parts. Also, threshold of given data by given local-FDR threshold 
is marked with dashed line. 

```{r}
# Density Estimation
plotSPMix(NN1d, testing = FALSE)
```

If testing is FALSE, it gives density estimation and classifies two parts(normal/nonparametric) by local-FDR value (local-FDR $> 0.5$?). 

### Normal + Gamma

What if alternative distribution is not normal?

$$f = 0.8 \cdot N(0,1) + 0.2 \cdot Gamma(shape = 12, rate = 4)$$

```{r}
z1_gamma <- rgamma(n1, shape = 12, rate = 4)
z_NG1d <- c(z0, z1_gamma)

NG1d <- SPMix(z_NG1d, thre = 0.35)
```

```{r}
# Hypothesis testing 
plotSPMix(NG1d)
```

```{r}
# Density Estimation
plotSPMix(NG1d, testing = FALSE)
```
Here’s a tight R Markdown section you can drop into your vignette. It explains **`thre`** and **`tol`**, gives **four example fits (top→bottom getting better)**, and a **simple tuning recipe**.


## Hyperparameter tuning

`SPMix` fits a two–component semiparametric mixture via EM. Let
\(\gamma_i^{(t)}=\Pr\{z_i\ \text{from alternative}\mid \text{current params at iter }t\}\)
be the posterior responsibility.

- **`thre`** (default 0.4) controls which points are treated as “alternative” in the **M-step** log-concave fit:
$$
  \mathbf{I}_{\text{alt}}^{(t)}=\{\,i:\ \gamma_i^{(t)}\ge \texttt{thre}\,\}.
$$
  - Smaller `thre` → include more ambiguous points → **smoother** but can **bias** the alternative density.
  - Larger `thre` → only high-confidence points → **sharper** but can be **high-variance**/spiky.
  - In practice for 1D z-like inputs, `thre ∈ [0.30, 0.45]` is a good starting band.

- **`tol`** is the EM **stopping tolerance**; the algorithm stops when
  \(\max_i |\gamma_i^{(t+1)}-\gamma_i^{(t)}|<\texttt{tol}\).
  - Larger `tol` (e.g., `1e-4`) → **fewer iterations**, slightly rougher convergence.
  - Smaller `tol` (e.g., `5e-5` or `1e-5`) → **tighter convergence**, more iterations; improvements are typically marginal beyond `~1e-5`.

Below, the fits improve **from top to bottom** as we move to a more suitable `thre` and then tighten `tol`.

```{r results='hide'}
# Example data 'z_NG1d' assumed constructed earlier; SPMix returns localFDR, f, f1, etc.

# 1) Too strict on alternative set → can be spiky
NG1d <- SPMix(z_NG1d, thre = 0.40)
plotSPMix(NG1d)
```

```{r results='hide'}
# 2) Too permissive → smoother but may wash out the alternative tail
NG1d <- SPMix(z_NG1d, thre = 0.20)
plotSPMix(NG1d)
```

```{r results='hide'}
# 3) Balanced threshold with moderate convergence tolerance
NG1d <- SPMix(z_NG1d, thre = 0.35, tol = 1e-4)
plotSPMix(NG1d)
```

```{r message=FALSE}
# 4) Same threshold, tighter convergence → typically the best of these four
NG1d <- SPMix(z_NG1d, thre = 0.35, tol = 5e-5)
plotSPMix(NG1d)
```

### How to adjust `thre` and `tol`

1. **Fix `tol`** at `1e-4` and **sweep `thre`** over a small grid, e.g., `{0.25, 0.30, 0.35, 0.40, 0.45}`.
   Pick the `thre` that yields:

   * stable null estimates $(\hat\mu_0,\hat\sigma_0)$,
   * a **credible** alternative density (no over-spiky bumps; tail behavior aligned with domain expectations),
   * smooth, monotone-sensible **localFDR** curves (e.g., decreasing along an alternative-dominated tail),
   * and (optionally) the best **held-out** log-likelihood.
2. **Tighten `tol`** to `5e-5` (or `1e-5` if iterations allow) **at the chosen `thre`**.
   Stop tightening once parameter changes, log-likelihood, and localFDR curves **visually stabilize** and EM iterations remain within your `max_iter`.
3. **Sanity checks** (report in the vignette):

   * EM **iterations** used vs. `max_iter` (convergence reached?).
   * **Sensitivity**: small perturbations of `thre` (±0.05) don’t materially change localFDR in the principal region.
   * **Downstream stability**: FDP/FDR control or discovery set doesn’t oscillate across nearby settings.

**Tip.** If you see jagged alternative densities or oscillatory localFDR, raise `thre` a little (to reduce noisy points) **or** increase `tol` slightly and/or increase `min_iter` so the EM stabilizes before stopping. If the alternative looks too flat and misses a clear tail, lower `thre` a touch.


## 2-dimensional data

### Normal + Gaussian Copula

```{r}
n = 500
p0 <- 0.8
n0 <- rbinom(1, n, p0)
n1 <- n - n0
sig0 <- matrix(c(1, 0.25, 0.25, 1), ncol = 2, byrow = T)
V <- rCopula(n1, ellipCopula(family = "normal", param = 0.5, dim = 2))
z0 <- rmvnorm(n0, sigma = sig0)
z1 <- qnorm(V, mean = 2.0, sd = .5)
z_NN2d <- data.frame(rbind(z0, z1))

ggplot(z_NN2d, aes(x = z_NN2d[,1], y = z_NN2d[,2])) +
  geom_point(aes(color = factor(c(rep(1,n0), rep(2,n1)), labels = c("Normal(Null)", "Gaussian Copula(Alternative)")))) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#999999", "#E69F00"), name="")  +
  labs(title = "Random Generated Mixture density data", x = "x", y = "y") +
  theme_classic()
```


```{r message=FALSE}
NN2d <- SPMix(z_NN2d)
plotSPMix(NN2d, coord_legend = c(4, -1, 0))
```

__plotSPMix()__ also provides visualization of 2-dimensional data.
You can set name for x-axis and y-axis using __xlab__, __ylab__. 

### Normal + Frank Copula

Let's consider nonnull distribution as Frank copula with marginal gamma distribution.

```{r results='hide'}
z1_gamma <- qgamma(V, shape = 12, rate = 4)
z_NG <- data.frame(rbind(z0, z1_gamma))
z1_gamma <- qgamma(V, shape = 10, rate = 4)
z_NG2d <- data.frame(rbind(z0, z1_gamma))

ggplot(z_NG, aes(x = z_NG[,1], y = z_NG[,2])) +
  geom_point(aes(color = factor(c(rep(1,n0), rep(2,n1)), labels = c("Normal", "Gamma")))) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#999999", "#E69F00"), name="")  +
  labs(title = "Random Generated Normal/Gamma Mixture", x="x", y = "y") +
  theme_classic()
```

```{r message=FALSE, results='hide'}
NG2d <- SPMix(z_NG)
plotSPMix(NG2d)
```

## 3-dimensional data

### Normal + Gaussian Copula

Let's consider null distribution and multivariate normal density and nonnull distribution as Gaussian copula with marginal normal distribution.

```{r}
library(scatterplot3d)

Sigma0 <- matrix(c(1, 0.25, 0.25, 0.25, 1, 0.25, 0.25,0.25,1), ncol = 3)
n0 <- rbinom(1, n, p0)
n1 <- n - n0
V <- rCopula(n1, ellipCopula(family = "normal", param = 0.5, dim = 3))
z0_NN3d <- rmvnorm(n0, sigma = Sigma0)
z1_NN3d <- qnorm(V, mean = 2.0, sd = .5)
z_NN3d <- rbind(z0_NN3d, z1_NN3d)

NN3d <- SPMix(z_NN3d)
```

```{r}
plotSPMix(NN3d, fdr_cutoff = 0.1, coord_legend = c(6, -5, 2))
```

Orange dots are given data with lower local-FDR (localFDR $< 0.1$).

### Normal + Frank Copula

```{r}
V_NG <- rCopula(n1, frankCopula(param = 0.5, dim = 3))
z0_NG3d <- rmvnorm(n0, sigma = Sigma0)
z1_NG3d <- qgamma(V_NG, shape = 10, rate = 4)
z_NG3d <- rbind(z0_NG3d, z1_NG3d)

NG3d <- SPMix(z_NG3d)
```

```{r}
plotSPMix(NG3d, fdr_cutoff = 0.1, coord_legend = c(6, -5, 2))
```

## Computational Time Comparison

We compared computational times for 2D and 3D implementations over $n = 100$ to $10{,}000$. Both showed **faster-than-exponential** growth, with 3D consistently slower and the gap widening as $n$ increased.

At $n = 10{,}000$, 2D took \~4.1 minutes (246 s) and 3D \~9 minutes (540 s). The log–log plot highlights steep scaling for large $n$, and 95% confidence intervals reflect slightly higher variability in 3D runs.

All computations were performed locally on an **Apple iMac with an M3 chip (8-core CPU, 10-core GPU), 32 GB unified RAM, running macOS Sequoia 15**.


# Applications

## Galaxy Velocity (Univariate)

Internal data 'galaxy' is a data frame including radial velocities of globular clusters of
M104 and Milky Way stars. It's known that Milky Way stars have much lower radial velocities.

```{r}
data("galaxy", package = "multiLocalFDR")
head(galaxy)
```

```{r}
z_galaxy <- galaxy$velocity
x_galaxy <- SPMix(z_galaxy, alternative = FALSE)
```

* z_galaxy: input data does not have to be z-values or p-values.
* alternative = "less": we know that velocities of M104 are much faster and 
follow Normal density. 

```{r}
plotSPMix(x_galaxy, testing = FALSE, xlab = "velocity(km/s)")
```

## Pathways (Multivariate)

Internal data 'pathways' is a list of significantly upregulated genes in three published studies: (1) peripheral leukocytes(L), (2) orbital inflammatory disease(O), and (3) sinus brushings(S) compared to healthy controls.

```{r}
data("pathways", package = "multiLocalFDR")
head(pathways)
```

### Univariate analysis

```{r eval=FALSE}
## SPMix for each pathway
x_L <- SPMix(pathways[,2], is_pvalue = TRUE)
x_O <- SPMix(pathways[,3], is_pvalue = TRUE)
x_S <- SPMix(pathways[,4], is_pvalue = TRUE)

## Plot results for each pathway
plotSPMix(x_L, xlab = "Peripheral Leukocytes")
plotSPMix(x_O, xlab = "Orbital Tissue")
plotSPMix(x_S, xlab = "Sinus Brushings")
```

```{r echo=FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics("/Users/user/Documents/GitHub/multiLocalFDR/tmp_figure/1dpath1.png")
knitr::include_graphics("/Users/user/Documents/GitHub/multiLocalFDR/tmp_figure/1dpath2.png")
knitr::include_graphics("/Users/user/Documents/GitHub/multiLocalFDR/tmp_figure/1dpath3.png")
```

### Multivariate Analysis

```{r eval=FALSE}
## SpMix for 3-dimensional data
params_LOS <- SPMix(pathways[,2:4], p_value = TRUE, tol = 1e-10)

## Pathways which md-fdr <= 0.01
head(pathways[params_LOS$localFDR <= 0.01,]$Gene.Set)
length(pathways[params_LOS$localFDR <= 0.01,]$Gene.Set)

# md-fdr dataframe
pathways_df <- pathways
pathways_df$localFDR <- params_LOS$localFDR
pathways_df$sgnf <- (params_LOS$localFDR <= 0.01)
head(pathways_df)

x_LOS <- SPMix(pathways[,2:4], p_value = TRUE)

## Pathways which md-fdr <= 0.01
head(pathways[x_LOS$localFDR <= 0.01,]$Gene.Set)
length(pathways[x_LOS$localFDR <= 0.01,]$Gene.Set)
```

## Two-sided testing via $\chi^2$ pivot: probit transform

For two-sided tests, map $z \mapsto z_{\chi}\ge 0$ using
$p = 1 - F_{\chi^2_1}(z^2)$, then $z_{\chi} = \Phi^{-1}(1-p) = \Phi^{-1}(F_{\chi^2_1}(z^2))$.
This gives a **right-tail** scale compatible with your one-sided `SPMix` (alternative in the right tail).

We start with Efron’s `policez` (z-statistics). A **two-sided** test has p-value
\(p_{2s} = 2\{1-\Phi(|z|)\}\). To use our **one-sided** `SPMix` (right-tail),
we convert two-sided evidence \(|z|\) to a **nonnegative z-like** statistic using a
\(\chi^2_1\) pivot:

\[
Q = z^2 \sim \chi^2_1\ \text{under }H_0,\qquad
p = 1 - F_{\chi^2_1}(Q),\qquad
z_{\chi} = \Phi^{-1}(1 - p) = \Phi^{-1}\!\big(F_{\chi^2_1}(z^2)\big)\ \ge 0.
\]

Intuition: large \(|z|\) ↔ large \(Q\) ↔ small \(p\) ↔ large \(z_{\chi}\) (right tail).  
We then fit `SPMix` to \(z_{\chi}\) with the alternative on the **right**.

## Police Data (Univariate z-scores)

This example uses the *police* z-score dataset from Efron (2010, §6.1) to illustrate a two-sided mixture fit with `SPMix`.

```{r echo=FALSE}
load("/Users/user/Documents/GitHub/multiLocalFDR/tmp_figure/policez.RData")
```


```{r}
# Two-sided → right-tailed, nonnegative z-like transform
z <- as.numeric(policez)
z_chi <- qnorm(pchisq(z^2, df = 1))   # = qnorm(2*pnorm(abs(z)) - 1); nonnegative

```

```{r }
z_chi <- z_chi[is.finite(z_chi)]      
hist(z_chi)
fit_z_chi <- SPMix(z_chi, thre = 0.15, tol = 5.0e-1,
                  Uthre_gam = 0.9, Lthre_gam = 0.1)
plotSPMix(fit_z_chi)
```


## HIV data (univariate z-values, base R)

We compare controls (cols 1–4) vs HIV (cols 5–8) per feature:
1) log2-transform, 2) compute two-sample pooled-variance t-statistics row-wise,
3) map t → z via the t CDF, 4) fit a two-sided mixture (`SPMix`).

```{r echo=FALSE}
load("/Users/user/Documents/GitHub/multiLocalFDR/tmp_figure/hivdata.RData")
```

```{r }
X <- as.matrix(hivdata)

# 1) log2-transform (add 1 to avoid log(0))
Xlog <- log2(X + 1)

# Indices and sizes
idx_ctrl <- 1:4
idx_hiv  <- 5:8
n1 <- length(idx_ctrl)
n2 <- length(idx_hiv)
df <- n1 + n2 - 2  # pooled t-test df = 6

# 2) row-wise pooled-variance t-statistics (vectorized)
m1   <- rowMeans(Xlog[, idx_ctrl, drop=FALSE])
m2   <- rowMeans(Xlog[, idx_hiv,  drop=FALSE])
s1sq <- apply(Xlog[, idx_ctrl, drop=FALSE], 1, var)  # sample var (n-1)
s2sq <- apply(Xlog[, idx_hiv,  drop=FALSE], 1, var)

sp2  <- ((n1 - 1)*s1sq + (n2 - 1)*s2sq) / df
tstat <- (m2 - m1) / sqrt(sp2 * (1/n1 + 1/n2))

# 3) map t → z with same (one-sided) tail prob
hivz <- qnorm(pt(tstat, df=df))

# Quick sanity check
summary(hivz)
hist(hivz, breaks=80, main="HIV z-values", xlab="z")

# 4) Fit two-sided SPMix (departures in both tails)
z_chi_hivz <- qnorm(pchisq(hivz^2, df = 1))

hist(z_chi_hivz)

fit_hivz <- SPMix(z = z_chi_hivz, thre = 0.14, tol = 5.0e-1,
                  Uthre_gam = 0.9, Lthre_gam = 0.1)
plotSPMix(fit_hivz)

```
